text: Navigate and manage files. Move, copy, rename, delete, find, and compress files and directories.
Search and read text and data. View, filter, and summarize files and logs, from a short config to a multi-gigabyte dataset.
Edit text and config. Change code, config files, and scripts without leaving the terminal.
Combine tools with pipes and redirection. Chain small commands so the output of one becomes the input of the next.
Automate with scripts and schedules. Save repeatable work as shell scripts and run it on a timer or trigger.
Write, build, and run code. Compile, test, and debug programs, and run scripts and jobs.
Manage processes and resources. Start, background, pause, and kill programs, and check CPU, memory, and disk use.
Run services and containers. Start servers, databases, and containers, and manage how they run.
Install and manage software. Add, update, and remove packages and libraries, and pin versions.
Manage users, permissions, and security. Control who can access what, and configure firewalls and network settings.
Monitor and troubleshoot. Read logs, diagnose faults, and test networks and system health.
Connect to other machines. Log in to remote servers, clusters, and devices over SSH or serial.
Transfer and fetch data. Download, upload, and sync files between machines and from the web.
Track and share code. Version your work and collaborate with Git.
Get help and tailor your environment. Use man pages and --help, and set up aliases, prompts, and shell config.
